discoveries.name: The wildflower meadow
discoveries.hint: about 36 steps east of the plaza
discoveries.finding: Seven kinds of flower grow here in bands by soil. The bees visit the yellow band first, in the cool of the morning.
notes: Soil core sampling reveals high calcium content near the yellow clover zone, explaining why bumblebees cluster there at dawn.
Purple vetch along the western fringe fixes nitrogen, gradually enriching the subsoil for surrounding grasses.
Flowering cycles shift precisely with daytime thermal currents, petals folding forty minutes before evening rainfall.
Seed pods disperse by wind vortexes formed by the ridge contour, scattering seeds thirty metres down-slope.

discoveries.name: The old boundary stone
discoveries.hint: about 44 steps north-west of the plaza
discoveries.finding: A worn stone, older than the village. Its lichen grows only on the north face, so it also tells you which way you face.
notes: Petrographic analysis identifies the rock as metamorphic granodiorite, deposited by prehistoric glacial melt.
Deep horizontal chisel grooves show consistent weathering patina, indicating placement at least three centuries ago.
The northern lichen crust consists of Xanthoria parietina, whose growth rate measures roughly two millimetres per season.
Local magnetic deviation near the stone is completely neutral, making it an ideal reference point for triangulation.

discoveries.name: The hidden spring
discoveries.hint: about 49 steps north-east of the plaza
discoveries.finding: Cold, clear water rises here all year. It feeds the well by an underground seam: the well is never really empty.
notes: Water temperature stays at a uniform seven degrees Celsius year-round, emerging through a pressurized limestone fissure.
Mineral filtration through alluvial gravel layers leaves zero detectable turbidity or iron precipitate.
Subterranean acoustic probes register an underground chamber roughly twelve metres below the outflow pool.
Freshwater amphipods inhabiting the dark spring pool indicate exceptional dissolved oxygen saturation.

discoveries.name: The high view
discoveries.hint: about 52 steps north of the plaza
discoveries.finding: From here the whole valley is a map: fields, the winding road, and where the next cottages could stand.
notes: Panoramic line-of-sight analysis confirms visual contact with both the eastern pass and the southern forest belt.
Wind speed at the bluff crest averages four metres per second stronger than at the plaza floor.
Thermal up-drafts along the south-facing rock slope provide effortless lift for soaring raptors every afternoon.
Bedrock fractures here show stable joint patterns, capable of bearing foundations for an extended survey outpost.

discoveries.name: The bee hollow
discoveries.hint: about 46 steps north of the plaza
discoveries.finding: A hollow oak hums with a colony. Keepers note the bees are calm unless smoke is near; the honey feeds the whole village.
notes: Internal hive temperature is regulated at thirty-four degrees through cooperative wing-fanning at the hollow entrance.
Pollen samples brought into the colony show foraging trips extending up to two kilometres into the clover fields.
Propolis resin harvested from poplar buds lines the hollow interior, preventing fungal rot in the aged heartwood.
The colony has wintered safely in this hollow for nine recorded seasons without requiring artificial feeding.

discoveries.name: The lichen wall
discoveries.hint: about 44 steps west of the plaza
discoveries.finding: Lichen draws a slow map on the stone. Researchers measure its growth each season; the clean air shows in its colours.
notes: Concentric growth rings on the central thallus suggest continuous symbiotic growth spanning over eighty years.
Spectroscopic readings show zero sulphur dioxide discoloration, serving as a reliable living barometer of air purity.
Moisture absorption happens directly through atmospheric condensation without requiring surface runoff.
Microscopic tardigrades inhabit the damp cushion layer, entering cryptobiosis during dry summer weeks.

discoveries.name: The birdsong grove
discoveries.hint: about 60 steps north-west of the plaza
discoveries.finding: At dawn eleven species sing in turn. Scholars are keeping a score of the chorus, one new voice a week.
notes: Acoustic frequency analysis reveals the chaffinch chorus peaks at four kilohertz, cutting cleanly through rustling leaves.
Deciduous canopy layering provides distinct vertical nesting tiers for seven non-competing songbird species.
Dawn chorus commencement tracks precisely with nautical twilight rather than local sunrise.
Seed-caching behaviour by nuthatches in oak bark fissures directly contributes to natural sapling regeneration.

discoveries.name: The clay bank
discoveries.hint: about 30 steps north-east of the plaza
discoveries.finding: Fine red clay, good for bricks and pots. Makers dig only what they need and smooth the bank behind them.
notes: Sedimentary stratification displays alternate layers of fine kaolinite clay and water-sorted quartz sand.
Plasticity testing proves the material can be thrown on a wheel without cracking at twenty percent moisture content.
High iron oxide content imparts a warm terracotta color upon kiln firing at nine hundred degrees.
Erosion along the excavated cut stabilizes naturally within three weeks when stepped at a forty-degree incline.

discoveries.name: The star meadow
discoveries.hint: about 46 steps south-east of the plaza
discoveries.finding: The darkest corner of Harr. On clear nights the observatory scholars chart the sky from here before the platform is done.
notes: Atmospheric scintillation measurements show minimal thermal turbulence, yielding Bortle class one sky clarity.
Surrounding woodland ridges create a natural light basin, shielding the meadow from peripheral ground reflections.
Nocturnal dew formation peaks before midnight, after which cool mountain breezes keep telescope optics dry.
Ground radiation cools rapidly after sunset due to low soil moisture and porous gravel underlayment.

discoveries.name: The wind ridge
discoveries.hint: about 35 steps south of the plaza
discoveries.finding: A steady breeze crosses this ridge. A small mill here could turn grain for the whole village; the plans are in the library.
notes: Anemometer logs show a continuous laminar airflow originating from the valley pressure gradient.
Wind vector consistency exceeds eighty percent from the south-southwest between midday and twilight.
Dwarf juniper shrubs along the crest exhibit flag-form growth, permanently shaped by prevailing air currents.
Aerodynamic pressure differentials across the saddle create an optimal funnel for small wind turbine placement.
